title: CD0066
description:
Plan submitted by: LeeNichols on 11/11/2021
USER DESCRIPTION: This map respects the Constitution, populations, continuity, communities of interest and competitiveness.   Additionally this map has also incorporated the desires of the City of Tucson Mayor and council to achieve a legislative seat to represent the good residents of the City of Tucson.
USER PLAN OBJECTIVE: This map of southern Arizona was made to respect the City of Tucson's Mayor's request to be included in the mandated Minority/Majority Congressional District.  (Currently labeled District 7.)  The Mayor is a strong proponent for the good citizens of the City of Tucson.

title: World Transit Stops
description:
This layer depicts the public transportation stops received through the Esri Community Maps program, USDOT, and publicly available datasets from agencies, municipalities and countries around the world. It is designed to be used with the other World Transit layers in the Living Alas. These layers include:
  • World Transit Agency Centroids
  • World Transit Lines by Modality
  • World Transit Lines by Agency Color
     
These transit layers can be accessed together through the following resources:
  • World Transit Group Layer
  • World Transit Web Map
  • World Transit Viewer (Web Mapping Application)


Stops are symbolized by their modality, such as bus, train, or funicular. If a stop serves multiple modalities (a station with trains and busses), the stop symbology prioritizes more permanent modes of transport, such as train over bus. 

The transit data is received in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format, an open data standard for public transportation data. Each GTFS dataset is a zipped archive of comma-separated files describing the transit services, including the geometry for mapping. Esri converts GTFS datasets into ready-to-use map layers and makes them available as Feature Services in the Living Atlas. Esri Transit map layers include data from Esri Community Maps contributors, the US Department of Transportation, as well as publicly available GTFS datasets.
 
Please note that any data layer fields marked with an "(Esri)" tag have been added by Esri to provide user-friendly translations of GTFS standard values or to add additional context and value.
 
 
Community Maps GTFS data

Through the Esri Community Maps Program, transit organizations are able to submit their own GTFS data for use across the ArcGIS platform, giving their data more visibility and accessibility to users. Organizations interested in sharing their data can join the Community Maps Program as a data contributor.
 
Community Maps transit contributors include:
